body:
## Module 2 in two minutes

**Building a course used to be expensive, and the expense was doing work nobody counted. It was the filter.** When a program cost six weeks, "this is a process problem" was an argument you could win — not because anyone valued diagnosis, but because the alternative was visibly costly and someone had to sign for it.

**Production time was doing three jobs nobody assigned it.** It was the economic filter that killed bad requests. It *forced the SME conversation*, which is where the real problem usually surfaced — never scheduled as diagnosis, it just happened because production required it. And it rationed volume, so choosing was necessary. Remove the cost and all three stop silently.

**The first cut is brutally simple: training fixes people who can't. It never fixes people who don't.** The test — could they do it tomorrow for a large enough reward? Training a willingness problem is worse than nothing, because it produces evidence the problem was handled and buys the real cause eighteen months of quiet.

**The request is a symptom report, not a specification.** The requester saw something real, then handed you their own amateur diagnosis. *"Tell me what you saw that made you think of training"* accepts the first and declines the second.

## The rule

**A refusal that only declines gets routed around — to someone who will build it by Friday.**

The shape that survives has three parts: what you found, what training would and wouldn't do, and **what you will own instead.** The third is load-bearing. A diagnosis that costs you nothing cannot be distinguished from avoidance, and the requester can tell.

## What the full module adds

Why L&D is structurally rewarded for collaboration and structurally unmeasured on diagnosis. The environmental-causes prior — **worth holding, not worth citing** — and an honest account of why its provenance looks exactly like the fabrications Module 3 dismantles. The SME-displacement argument in full. Four requests to sort, only one of which is actually a training problem. And the activity: one live request from your own queue, taken apart, with *"this isn't a training problem"* and its opposite both genuinely available.
